change: the tectum subtracts the optic flow the animal's OWN motion predicts, from an efference copy of its yaw rate and forward speed, before looking for anything

detection_vs_range_animal_still.method: animal held stationary, prey wiggling dead ahead, 40 frames per range
detection_vs_range_animal_still.reading: it responds at EVERY range tested, including where the prey covers half a cell. Resolution was never the limit.

moving_vs_still_during_a_real_hunt.reading: the effect finally points the right way -- the eye sees more when the animal is still. Before the efference copy it pointed the wrong way (d = -0.128 and -0.212).

what_is_still_wrong: Detection during a real hunt is weak in absolute terms. The controlled test reaches peak salience 0.67-0.83 with the animal stationary and prey wiggling ahead; in a hunt the same eye averages 0.02. The gap is that prey is often out of view or not moving on a given frame. The oracle has NOT been removed and must not be until this closes.
the_architecture_this_points_at: Look while still, move while blind. A stalking predator freezes to look, and the creep this project already implements -- move one step in four -- happens to be exactly that. The detector should be read during the pauses, not continuously.
